name: Congenital Pulmonary Lymphangiectasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Histological evidence of dilated pulmonary lymphatic vessels in lung tissue
Neonatal respiratory distress with persistent chylous pleural effusions
Radiologic findings of interstitial thickening and pleural effusions on chest imaging
Exclusion of secondary causes of pulmonary lymphangiectasia such as cardiac anomalies or lymphatic obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus histopathological confirmation or consistent imaging findings with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is often required for definitive diagnosis; prenatal diagnosis possible via fetal ultrasound or MRI in some cases

laboratory: Chylous pleural fluid analysis showing high triglycerides and lymphocytes
imaging: Chest X-ray showing bilateral pleural effusions and interstitial infiltrates
High-resolution CT scan demonstrating diffuse interstitial thickening and lymphatic dilatation
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Rare familial cases reported suggesting possible genetic predisposition
other: Histopathology revealing dilated lymphatic vessels in the pulmonary interstitium and pleura

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of underlying cardiac or lymphatic obstruction
Later onset compared to congenital form
Absence of lymphatic vessel dilation on histology
History of trauma or thoracic surgery

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress unresponsive to conventional therapy
Persistent chylous pleural effusions despite drainage
Rapid progression to respiratory failure in neonate
references: Noonan JA, et al. Congenital pulmonary lymphangiectasia: clinical and pathological features. Am J Med Genet. 1994.
Dori Y, et al. Pulmonary lymphatic disorders: diagnosis and management. Pediatr Radiol. 2017.
Orphanet: Congenital pulmonary lymphangiectasia. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
